# opencode-enhanced

> A fork of opencode (the open source AI coding agent) that adds a tokens/second
> performance indicator, a tool-free `chat` agent mode, and browser automation
> via Playwright and system Chrome. Aimed at developers running local or
> self-hosted LLMs, and at anyone who wants a browser-capable coding agent
> without a closed-source IDE.

opencode-enhanced is a small distribution layered on upstream opencode. It is not a
rewrite: nearly all code is upstream's, and the fork's own diff spans three
files. It is designed to be cheap to rebase as upstream moves.

## What it adds

- **Tokens/second indicator.** A live tok/s, token count, and elapsed-time
  readout pinned above the TUI input while generating, plus a final figure on
  each completed message. Intended for self-hosted inference (Ollama, vLLM,
  llama.cpp, LM Studio), where generation speed reveals quantisation problems,
  VRAM spill-over into system RAM, and context-length costs that are otherwise
  invisible. Always on, no configuration.

- **`chat` agent mode.** A preset with every tool disabled and every permission
  set to deny, producing a plain conversational assistant. Exists because many
  capable local and uncensored models either lack tool-calling support entirely
  or do it so unreliably that an agent loop derails. Configured in
  `opencode.json` under `agent.chat`.

- **Browser automation.** Setting `OPENCODE_BROWSER_AUTOMATION=1` auto-registers
  Microsoft's official `@playwright/mcp` server, giving the agent real browser
  control, navigate, click, fill forms, read rendered pages, with no manual
  MCP setup. Uses system-installed Chrome by default and runs headed by default.
  Additional switches: `OPENCODE_BROWSER_HEADLESS`,
  `OPENCODE_BROWSER_SYSTEM_CHROME`. Ported from Kilo Code, which implements its
  browser agent the same way. This makes opencode-enhanced a viable open, self-hosted
  alternative to browser-agent IDEs such as Google Antigravity.

## Bring your own key (BYOK)

Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works through the `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible`
adapter, so hosted APIs and local servers are configured identically, Ollama,
vLLM, LM Studio, OpenRouter, Together, and similar. Providers are declared in
`opencode.json`; API keys live in `~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json` and are
never committed.

## Key facts

- Language: TypeScript, built with Bun; compiles to a standalone binary.
- Build: `bun install && bun run --cwd packages/opencode build --single`
- macOS caveat: re-sign with `codesign --force --sign - <binary>` after copying
  a Bun-compiled binary, or it is SIGKILLed with exit code 137.
- License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, source-available, free for
  noncommercial use, **not** OSI-approved open source. Upstream opencode and
  Kilo Code remain MIT and can be used commercially from their own repositories.

## Upstream and attribution

- opencode, <https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode> (MIT), the base agent.
- Kilo Code, <https://github.com/Kilo-Org/kilocode> (MIT), browser automation
  approach; itself an opencode derivative.
- Playwright MCP, <https://github.com/microsoft/playwright-mcp>, performs the
  actual browser automation.
